blocks.content: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.

rows: Parliament (via Presidential order after address by Parliament)
Same as a Supreme Court Judge (Special Majority)

items: Exam Trap: The CEC does NOT hold office during the pleasure of the President, even though appointed by the President.
Crucial Point: Other Election Commissioners are removed by the President ONLY on the recommendation of the CEC.
Removal Procedure: Requires a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament supported by a special majority.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is provided with security of tenure and does not hold office at the pleasure of the President.
The CEC can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
The grounds for removal are limited to proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Other Election Commissioners or Regional Commissioners cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Service conditions of the CEC cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
